cover.headline: The gRevlimid hangover is in the price; the inhaler relaunch in the US and the Indian franchise are not. Patience required
cover.lead: Cipla is one of India's three largest drug makers and its respiratory leader (26% of the Indian respiratory market), with half its revenue in India, a quarter in the US and the rest in Africa, emerging markets and Europe. Its profit fell 26% in FY26 when a US windfall ended: a generic of the blood-cancer drug Revlimid, sold under a settlement that kept prices high, stopped in the December 2025 quarter, and its lanreotide partner's plant was barred from the US. Q1FY27 EBITDA margin was 16.7% (25.6% a year earlier) and US revenue $162mn a quarter, against management's goal of a $1bn annual run-rate by March 2027. The stock has moved {{P.returns.1y|chg}} in a year to ₹1,346: 28.9x our FY27E EPS and 22.4x FY28E, with ₹9,494 cr of net cash. The street values Cipla on **P/E on FY28E EPS (19-25x)**. We forecast EPS of ₹46.6 / 60.2 / 65.9 for FY27-29E, below the street: our US build is more cautious than management's. Applying **26.5x to Sep-28E EPS of ₹63.1** (Cipla's own forward median on EPS before exceptional items, 24.5x, re-rated by the pharma sector's +7.5%) gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹1,511, DCF ₹1,090; the DCF is the warning. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: India is the anchor, and it is accelerating
arguments.p: One India (₹12,680 cr, 45% of revenue) grew 12.4% in Q1FY27, the prescription business 15.4% (183bp ahead of the market). Cipla owns Indian respiratory (Foracort is the country's No.1 inhaler brand at ~₹1,070 cr), is the largest company by volume, runs the biggest trade-generics network and added Eli Lilly's tirzepatide (Yurpeak, ~₹80 cr in its first full quarter). We model India at +11% / +10% / +10%.

arguments.h: The US cliff is behind; the relaunch depends on approvals
arguments.p: North America fell from $250mn a quarter (Q1FY25) to $162mn. The rebuild is in complex inhalers and peptides: gVentolin (approved Apr-2026, six months of exclusivity), gAdvair (approved 27-Jul-2026, but with three or four rivals), gSymbicort, a third inhaler and a first-to-file peptide still pending. We model $775mn / $900mn / $920mn for FY27-29E, below management's ~$1bn exit run-rate, because Pithampur (seven USFDA observations in Aug-2026) and competition keep slipping the timeline.

arguments.h: Margins bottomed in Q4FY26; EPS should rebound ~30% in FY28
arguments.p: We model EBITDA margins of {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.1|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}}: the bottom of the 18.5-20% FY27 guidance, then back to the pre-windfall ~21% as high-margin in-house inhalers fill US plants that are already staffed. FY28E EPS (₹60.2) is 12% below ICICI Direct and 15% below Elara, whose FY28 includes a one-off first-to-file exclusivity.

arguments.h: Valuation: fair to cheap on history, expensive on cash flows
arguments.p: At 22.4x FY28E Cipla trades below its 24.5x forward median since 2021, while pharma peers trade ~8% above their own five-year medians. That gives 26.5x and {{dcf.tp|inr}}. But ROE is ~12% against an 11.3% cost of equity and the DCF says ₹1,090: the target needs the launches to arrive and the market to keep paying a growth multiple for them.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the first quarter with gAdvair and a ramping gVentolin; margin against the 18.5-20% guidance.
USFDA approvals for gSymbicort, the third respiratory asset (filed from Goa) and the first-to-file peptide, all expected in FY27.
Pithampur: Cipla's response to the seven observations of Aug-2026 and the site classification; the warning letter has been in place since Nov-2023.
Competition: gVentolin's six-month exclusivity runs out around the end of 2026; the number of gAdvair rivals.
Lanreotide: partner remediation or the alternate US site (filing targeted by Q4FY27); use of ₹9,500 cr of net cash.

sections.title: What Cipla does: India's inhaler company, with a US generics arm and an African franchise

blocks.p: Cipla makes and sells medicines in ~70 countries from 48 plants. It has four businesses. **One India** (₹12,680 cr in FY26, 45% of revenue) sells branded prescription drugs through ~12,000 medical representatives, unbranded "trade generics" through 15,000+ stockists to chemists, and consumer brands (Nicotex, Omnigel, Cipladine). **North America** ($780mn, 24%) sells generics in the US: albuterol inhalers (No.1, 21% share), injectables such as lanreotide (until supply stopped), and until Dec-2025 generic Revlimid. **One Africa** ($483mn, 15%) is mainly South Africa, where Cipla is the No.2 prescription company, plus tenders and global-access sales of HIV and malaria drugs. **Emerging Markets & Europe** ($405mn, 13%) sells under its own brand or through partners. Respiratory drugs are about a third of group revenue.

sections.title: Industry: India is growing faster; US generics pay only for complexity

blocks.p: **India.** Indian pharma market (IPM): +13.5% in Q1FY27 and +11.1% on MAT Jun-26 (IQVIA, via Kotak Neo); Pharmarack: Jun-2026 +13.3%, MAT +9.8%. Chronic therapies grew ~20% in Jun-2026 vs ~13% for acute. Obesity and diabetes (GLP-1s) are the fastest-growing segments. Cipla's prescription business grew 15.4% in the June quarter, 183bp ahead of the IPM (IQVIA). Growth is now led by chronic diseases (diabetes, heart, obesity) and by price increases on non-controlled drugs; acute drugs such as antibiotics and cough syrups depend on the season. Respiratory is a ~₹19,000-20,000 cr market (Cipla's ₹5,000 cr+ is 26% of it) growing low double digits, where inhalers replace tablets slowly as doctors and patients learn to use them; this is Cipla's home ground.

**United States.** US generics: price erosion in plain orals; value sits in complex products (inhalers, peptides, injectables) where few companies can make an approvable copy. Cipla's US share is 1.57% of generics, top-20 (AR FY26). Exclusivity windows are short: Advair already has three or four generic competitors; Ventolin has CGT exclusivity for six months. The money is in products that few companies can copy: inhalers need a device, a formulation and clinical studies; long-acting injectables and peptides need specialised plants. Approval depends as much on plant inspections as on the science, which is why Pithampur matters.

**Africa and other markets.** South African private market +5.7% (IQVIA MAT May-26); Cipla is No.2 in prescriptions (8.8% share) and No.3 overall (8.5%). Public tenders are price-driven: Cipla lost one in FY26 that hurts FY27. Emerging Markets & Europe: $405mn in FY26, direct-to-market (DTM) plus B2B; hit by the West Asia conflict in Q4FY26 ($90mn vs $103mn).

blocks.callout: **Our view:** Cipla captures the Indian growth tailwind well: its share of India in revenue rose from 40% to 45% in five years and its Rx business is beating the market. The US is not a tailwind but a series of bets. The weaker rupee is a real, if unglamorous, help: every ₹1 move in the rupee against the dollar changes FY28E revenue by ~₹150-200 cr (the US, Africa and other markets are priced in dollars or local currencies).

sections.title: One India: the inhaler franchise and a market-beating Q1 (+12.4%)

blocks.p: One India sells through three channels. **Branded prescriptions (Rx)** are the core: a ₹9,500 cr+ portfolio (AR FY26), 33 brands above ₹100 cr and 23 in the top 300 of the Indian market. Cipla is No.1 in respiratory, No.2 in urology and No.7 in cardiac. **Trade generics** (unbranded, sold to chemists through stockists) is India's largest such business: 15,000+ stockists, 150,000+ chemists, 7 brands above ₹50 cr. **Consumer health** (₹1,690 cr in FY26; ₹481 cr in Q1FY27) sells Nicotex, Omnigel and Cipladine, each No.1 in its segment. Growth slowed to 6-7% in H1FY26 (weak acute season, a muted Rx quarter) and recovered to 15% in Q4FY26 and 12% in Q1FY27.

blocks.p: Cipla holds ~26% of Indian respiratory (CARE) and its respiratory sales in the market crossed ₹5,000 cr (IQVIA MAT Dec-25). Four of its top ten brands are inhaled medicines: Foracort (budesonide-formoterol, ~₹1,070 cr, +16%), Duolin (~₹660 cr), Budecort (~₹580 cr) and Seroflo (~₹300 cr), plus Asthalin. The advantage is not the molecules, which are old, but 30 years of devices (Rotahaler, Synchrobreathe, Ciphaler), doctor education and patient habits. Rivals have sold inhalers in India for years without denting that lead. Respiratory is about one third of Cipla's group revenue.

bullets: **Organic vs bought growth.** In-licensed products are 10-15% of One India (CEO). Elara estimates organic growth at ~8% in Q1FY27 after the Pfizer brands, Yurpeak (~₹80 cr) and Inzpera; ICICI Direct puts in-licensing at ~1.5pp of Rx growth. Either way, Cipla's own portfolio grows a little below the market.
**Productivity, not headcount.** The field force is ~12,000 with no additions planned in FY27, after two years of hiring.
**Price control.** Many respiratory and anti-infective drugs are under India's price-control list (DPCO); price increases are capped at the wholesale-price index each April.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** One India is the best part of Cipla and the reason the stock holds a premium multiple. We model +11% / +10% / +10% (FY27-29E), in line with management's "double-digit, market-beating" guidance, taking India to 46.1% of group revenue by FY29E.

sections.title: North America: the windfall is gone; inhalers and a peptide must rebuild it

blocks.p: Cipla's US business has three layers. The **base**: 186 approved ANDAs and NDAs (incl. partners, Jun-2026), led by albuterol inhalers (No.1, 21% share, 50mn+ inhalers supplied), plus solid orals from InvaGen (New York) and injectables. The **windfall**: generic Revlimid, approved in Sep-2022 and sold under a settlement that capped generic volumes until 31-Jan-2026, so prices stayed high; Cipla shipped most of its last volumes in the Sep-2025 quarter, a little in Dec-2025 and none after. It never disclosed the revenue. And **lanreotide**, a long-acting injectable made by partner Pharmathen in Greece: production stopped after a Nov-2025 inspection and the plant was put under a USFDA import alert in Apr-2026. Together, these explain the fall from $250mn a quarter (Q1FY25) to $155mn (Q4FY26).

blocks.p: **One Africa** ($483mn in FY26, +7%) is mostly South Africa, where Cipla bought Medpro in 2013 and is now No.2 in prescriptions (8.8% share) and No.3 overall (8.5%), with 10 brands above ZAR100mn and the most top-100 generic brands. It crossed $400mn in FY26 but was hit by the West Asia conflict in Q4FY26 ($90mn vs $103mn a year earlier) and recovered to $106mn (+5%) in Q1FY27.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Cipla has one genuine moat, Indian respiratory, and a strong position in Indian distribution and South Africa. In the US it has capability (inhalers, peptides) but no lasting advantage: each product earns well for a few years until competitors arrive, and plant problems (Pithampur, Pharmathen) have repeatedly cost it launches. So the right way to think about Cipla is a high-quality Indian franchise with a US option attached, not a compounding global specialty company.

sections.title: Revenue doubled since FY19; profit tripled to FY25 on a US windfall, then fell 26% in FY26

blocks.p: Cipla's revenue grew from ₹16,362 cr in FY19 to ₹28,163 cr in FY26 (8% a year). Profit attributable to shareholders grew much faster, from ₹1,528 cr to a peak of ₹5,273 cr in FY25 (23% a year), and then fell to ₹3,879 cr in FY26. The reason is one product. From late 2022 Cipla sold a generic copy of Revlimid (lenalidomide, a blood-cancer drug) in the US under a settlement that capped how much generic makers could sell, so prices stayed high. In FY24-25 it was very profitable. It ended in the December 2025 quarter, and US revenue fell from $233mn in Q2FY26 to $155mn in Q4FY26. India, Africa and Europe kept growing, but not fast enough to fill the gap.

blocks.p: Cipla's EBITDA margin (operating profit before other income) fell 920bp (basis points; 100bp = 1 percentage point) between FY25 and Q1FY27. More than half came from gross margin: gRevlimid and lanreotide were high-margin, and Q1FY27 also carried war-related costs (1-2% of revenue, management) and higher-than-usual inventory write-offs. The rest came from people: employee cost rose from 17.5% of revenue to 21.0% because Cipla staffed its US plants and added field force ahead of launches that have not yet arrived. R&D went from 5.5% of revenue (FY25) to 7.0% (FY26).

sections.title: Returns: ROIC fell from 33% to 23%; cash keeps piling up

blocks.p: Cipla generated ₹13,079 cr of operating cash in FY24-26 and spent ₹5,976 cr on capex (including intangibles and in-licensing upfronts), ₹487 cr on acquisitions and ₹3,028 cr on dividends. The rest went into cash and liquid funds. Capex doubled in FY26 to ₹3,079 cr (new US inhaler and peptide capacity, in-licensed brands); management says the cycle should ease "after another year or so". The company's own return on invested capital (ROIC) was 33.1% in FY25 and 22.9% in FY26; return on equity was 11.8% in FY26 because ~₹10,500 cr of cash earns ~6%.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean accounts; watch exceptional items, intangibles and the new revenue presentation

bullets: **New revenue presentation (from Apr-2026).** Certain marketing and promotional spend is now deducted from revenue rather than shown as an expense. Q1FY27 growth was 2.3% reported vs ~4% like-for-like, mostly in South Africa. EBITDA is unchanged; the margin is slightly flattered.

**Exceptional items recur, in different forms.** FY23: goodwill impairment (cqcil held for sale rs39 cr, yemen cgu and others) (₹182 cr); FY24: pulmazole (pulmatrix) intangible impairment rs183.19 cr + wind-down rs11.63 cr (₹195 cr); FY26: new labour codes (gratuity and leave, from 21-nov-2025) (₹276 cr); FY26: impairment of investment in associates (shown above pbt) (₹42 cr). Each is genuinely one-off, so we use EPS before them for the valuation history (see Valuation).

**Other income is large and partly one-off.** FY26 other income was ₹882 cr (16% of pre-tax profit): ₹648 cr of treasury income (deposit interest and mutual-fund gains), ₹83 cr of recurring items and ₹151 cr of one-offs (FX gains, litigation settlement, asset-sale gains). Screener nets the ₹276 cr labour-code charge against it (₹606 cr). We build it from its parts (see Forecasts).

**Intangibles are rising.** Goodwill and intangibles went from ₹4,986 cr to ₹6,850 cr in FY26 as in-licensed brands and products were capitalised; amortisation will rise, and impairments (as with Pulmazole in FY24) are possible.
**Cash conversion.** Operating cash flow was ₹3,940 cr in FY26, 67% of EBITDA (after tax and working capital); inventory days rose to 252. Free cash flow was only ₹861 cr after ₹3,079 cr of capex.

**Contingent liability.** NPPA (drug-price regulator) overcharging claims since 1998: ₹2,011 cr (₹863 cr principal plus interest) under litigation, not provided (CARE). It is ~₹25 a share; we do not deduct it, but it is a tail risk.
**Minorities.** Small (a ₹17 cr loss absorbed in FY26). We use profit attributable to shareholders throughout (patch to Screener's net-profit row).
**Audit.** Walker Chandiok & Co (Grant Thornton Bharat), unqualified opinion for FY26.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** Simple and well disclosed: business-wise revenue every quarter, R&D expensed (7% of revenue), net cash. The traps are presentational: other income and exceptional items move reported EPS by 3-6% a year, and the revenue presentation changed in FY27.

sections.title: Balance sheet: ₹10,500 cr of net cash; working capital is the weak spot

blocks.p: Cipla has no meaningful debt: ₹614 cr at Mar-2026, mostly lease liabilities (₹356 cr) and small local borrowings. Against this it held ₹11,140 cr of cash, current investments (debt mutual funds) and bank deposits, so net cash was ₹10,526 cr (₹9,494 cr at Jun-2026 after the ₹1,050 cr dividend). Goodwill and intangibles rose to ₹6,850 cr (₹4,986 cr a year earlier) as Cipla capitalised in-licensed brands and products. The weak spot is working capital: inventory was 252 days of cost in FY26 (217 in FY24), as Cipla built stocks for launches and South African tenders.

sections.title: Our honest summary: own the Indian franchise and the US option, but size it for the DCF

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's respiratory leader and a top-three domestic franchise growing ~10-12%, a solid South African business, ~₹9,500 cr of net cash, and a US business that is rebuilding from a windfall-driven peak with a credible inhaler and peptide pipeline. Accounts are clean; the family is a minority holder and the company is professionally run.

**What you are paying:** 22.4x our FY28E EPS and 21.3x Sep-28E, below Cipla's 24.5x forward median, at a time when pharma peers trade above theirs. On the street's method and our (below-street) inputs the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): a BUY. The DCF (₹1,090) is the counter-argument: on cash flows alone the stock is fully priced, so the upside depends on the US launches arriving and on the market continuing to pay a growth multiple for pharma.

exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
Meaning
rows: Abbreviated New Drug Application (a generic) / New Drug Application, filed with the USFDA.
Active pharmaceutical ingredient: the drug substance itself, sold to other formulators.
Competitive Generic Therapy: 180 days of exclusivity for the first approved generic of a drug with little generic competition (gVentolin).
Long-term treatments (diabetes, heart, respiratory maintenance) vs short-term ones (antibiotics, cough and cold).
India's Drug Price Control Order and the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority that enforces it.
Dry-powder inhaler (e.g. Advair Diskus) / metered-dose inhaler (e.g. Ventolin, Symbicort).
Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation; here always excluding other income (company definition).
Enterprise value (market value plus debt minus cash) divided by EBITDA.
The first generic applicant challenging a patent, which can earn 180 days of exclusivity.
USFDA inspection observations / Voluntary Action Indicated (minor) / Official Action Indicated (serious) / formal letter that blocks new approvals from a site until fixed.
Share price divided by the next full fiscal year's EPS.
Generic lenalidomide (Revlimid, a blood-cancer drug), sold in the US under volume-limited settlements until 31-Jan-2026.
USFDA order stopping products from a plant entering the US (Pharmathen, Apr-2026).
Selling another company's product under licence (Yurpeak from Eli Lilly, Pfizer brands).
Indian pharmaceutical market / the data provider that tracks pharmacy-level (secondary) sales.
A small protein-like drug (liraglutide, teduglutide); complex to copy, so few generics.
Production-Linked Incentive: a government subsidy tied to output of eligible products.
Return on equity (profit ÷ shareholders' funds) / return on invested capital (operating profit after tax ÷ capital used in the business, excluding cash).
The median of pharma peers' P/E at 30-Sep-2026 vs their five-year medians (+7.5% for Cipla), applied to Cipla's own historical multiple.
Half of FY28E EPS plus half of FY29E EPS: the twelve-month-forward EPS the market will look at in September 2027, when the target falls due.
Unbranded generics sold to chemists through stockists, without doctor promotion.

A windfall (gRevlimid) is real operating profit from a temporary market position; a one-off (impairment, labour-code charge) is a non-operating item. House rule: windfalls stay in the valuation history, one-offs are taken out.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Cipla (consolidated, ₹ crore; profit attributable to shareholders, see tools/authoring/CIPLA.patch.js). Cipla reports one operating segment (pharmaceuticals) and revenue by customer location (India, USA, One Africa, Rest of world: AR FY26 note 53), so the engine runs on one revenue-growth path and one EBITDA-margin path; the business-line build (US revenue built in US dollars x an assumed rupee rate) sits in `businessLines` and the authoring script checks that it sums to model revenue. Other income = treasury yield x opening net cash on the company's basis (Screener cash and investments + bank deposits in other financial assets - non-current strategic investments - borrowings incl. leases: Rs10,526 cr at Mar-26) + recurring non-treasury income. Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Built by business (see businessLines; the script checks the sum). FY27E +8.9%: One India +11% (Q1 +12.4%, ~8% organic per Elara; management guides double-digit, market-beating growth for FY27-28; Yurpeak ~Rs80 cr in Q1); North America $775mn (FY26 $780mn; Q1 $162mn; we assume $180 / 205 / 228mn in Q2-Q4 as gVentolin ramps, gAdvair (approved 27-Jul-2026) launches in Q2 and one or two of gSymbicort, the third respiratory asset and the peptide (gGattex per Nomura and Elara) arrive in H2: below management's $1bn exit run-rate, which needs ~$250mn in Q4); rupee at Rs94.5/$ (Q1: Rs1,532 cr / $162mn = Rs94.6). One Africa +5.4% in rupees (flat in dollars: the lost South African tender weighs on the next three quarters and marketing spend is now netted from revenue). Rest of world +10% (EMEU +5% in dollars in Q1, API +57%, weaker rupee). Reported growth carries a ~2pp drag from the new revenue presentation (Q1 +2.3% reported, ~4% like-for-like). FY28E +11.4%: full year of the FY27 launches, possible gDovato first-to-file exclusivity (Elara) and partial return of lanreotide; US $900mn at Rs96.5. FY29E +8.0%: US $920mn (price erosion on FY27 launches as competitors enter) at Rs98.5; India +10%.

businessLines._why: Revenue by customer location, AR FY26 note 53 (FY26: India Rs12,680 cr, USA Rs6,872 cr, One Africa Rs4,285 cr, Rest of world Rs4,325 cr = Rs28,163 cr). US revenue is modelled in dollars (FY26 North America $780mn = Rs88.1/$ on the USA line) and converted at an assumed rupee rate that weakens ~2% a year from Rs94.5/$ in FY27E (Q1FY27: Rs94.6/$).

assumptions._marginWhy: Company-defined EBITDA margin (excluding other income): 25.9% (FY25), 21.0% (FY26), 16.7% in Q1FY27 (25.6% a year earlier) after gRevlimid ended (last shipments in the Dec-2025 quarter), lanreotide stopped (partner Pharmathen's Greek plant under a USFDA import alert since Apr-2026), war-related costs of 1-2% of revenue and launch costs already in the base. Guidance: 18.5-20% for FY27, H2-weighted and 'predicated on the launches' (CFO, 23-Jul-2026); '20 plus' should be sustained after that (CFO, 13-May-2026). FY27E 18.5%: the bottom of the range, because Q1 was 16.7% and our US build is below management's. FY28E 21.0%: full year of high-margin in-house respiratory launches (gAdvair, gVentolin, gSymbicort), India chronic mix, R&D held at ~7% of sales. FY29E 21.0%: US price erosion offset by India operating leverage. Each 1pp of margin is ~Rs340 cr of EBITDA (~5% of FY28E EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex (incl. intangibles and in-licensing upfronts): Rs1,349 / 1,548 / 3,079 cr in FY24-26 (Screener cash flow). The CFO said capex 'will probably reduce after another year or so because we've built enough capacity' (13-May-2026); Board approved up to $100mn for InvaGen capex and working capital (19-Mar-2026). We take Rs2,000 cr in FY27E and Rs1,600 cr a year after; acquisitions and in-licensing beyond that are not modelled.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation and amortisation Rs1,211 cr (excl. the Rs42 cr impairment of associates) = 5.6% of average gross block (Rs21,488 cr); Q1FY27 Rs304 cr (Rs1,217 cr annualised). The engine depreciates capex at once while CWIP is held flat, so we use 5.2%: FY27E ~Rs1,270 cr.

otherTreasury._why: Company net cash at Mar-26 = Rs11,140 cr of cash, current investments and fixed deposits less Rs614 cr of borrowings and leases = Rs10,526 cr (Q4FY26 presentation). Screener counts cash Rs1,307 cr and investments Rs8,223 cr, which include Rs544 cr of non-current strategic investments and associates that are not treasury, and misses Rs2,154 cr of bank deposits held in other financial assets (AR FY26 notes 9 and 18). Net adjustment +Rs1,610 cr (= 2,154 - 544), so the model's opening net cash equals the company's Rs10,526 cr.

assumptions._treasuryWhy: FY26 treasury income Rs648 cr (bank-deposit interest Rs174.8 cr + gains on sale of current investments Rs344.8 cr + fair-value gains Rs128.1 cr, AR FY26 note 32) on average net cash of ~Rs10,450 cr = 6.2% (FY25: Rs646 cr, ~7.1% on lower cash). We use 6.25% on opening net cash: Rs658 cr in FY27E on Rs10,526 cr.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Recurring non-treasury other income only (AR FY26 note 32): other interest Rs31.5 cr, rent Rs6.9 cr, government grants Rs0.8 cr and miscellaneous income Rs44.1 cr = Rs83 cr. Left out as one-offs (Rs151 cr in FY26): FX gain Rs52.5 cr, litigation settlement income Rs35.6 cr, gain on asset sales Rs31.8 cr, SEZ land settlement interest Rs21.6 cr, insurance claims, balances written back and tax-refund interest. FY27E total other income ~Rs743 cr vs Rs882 cr in FY26 (company) and Rs834 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 before the labour-code charge (Screener nets that exceptional item against other income: Rs558 cr); the gap is the one-offs and the Rs1,050 cr dividend paid in Q1FY27.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs54 cr; Q1FY27 Rs17 cr (Rs68 cr annualised). Debt is Rs600 cr including leases (Jun-26).
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective tax rate 25.9% in FY26 and 27.3% in Q1FY27 (22.4% in FY25 after deferred-tax credits). 26%: India at the 25.2% concessional rate, the US and South Africa higher, plus a small share of associate losses.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs13 a share (Rs1,050 cr, paid in Q1FY27) = 27% of EPS; FY25 Rs16 incl. a Rs3 special. Management prefers to keep cash for R&D, biosimilars and acquisitions (Q4FY26 call).

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash, AAA-rated, half the business in Indian branded generics; but US earnings swing with approvals, plant inspections and exclusivities. Ke 11.3%.
dcf._tgWhy: 5.5%: Indian pharma grows ~10% nominal, US generics low single digit in dollars; a blend near 5.5% in rupees.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~8% to 7% (India ~10%, US flattish, Africa and EMEU mid-single digit plus a weaker rupee).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Holds at 21%, the pre-gRevlimid level (FY22) and management's 'sustainable 20 plus'; no new windfall is assumed.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex settles at 4.5% of revenue (FY24-25 average ~5.5% incl. intangibles; FY26 11% was a peak); depreciation 4% of revenue (FY26 4.3%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Management delivers the $1bn US exit run-rate: gAdvair, gSymbicort and the peptide arrive on time with limited competition, gDovato exclusivity lands in FY28 and lanreotide returns; India keeps growing in the low teens.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: US approvals slip (Pithampur's seven observations and InvaGen's 483 delay filings), competitors enter gVentolin and gAdvair quickly, the South African tender loss and war costs persist; US revenue stays near $650-700mn.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Cipla: P/E on FY28E EPS (ICICI Direct 24x, Axis 25x, ICICI Securities 23x in Apr-2026, Elara 19x core EPS plus cash). 26.5x = Cipla's 24.5x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 on EPS before exceptional items (FY23 goodwill impairment, FY24 Pulmazole impairment, FY26 labour-code charge and associate impairment; 26.1x on reported EPS; no trough years: forward EPS never fell below half its prior three-year peak; gRevlimid is a windfall, not a one-off, so it stays in), times the pharma sector factor of 1.075 (median of SUNPHARMA, DIVISLAB, TORNTPHARM, ZYDUSLIFE, AUROPHARMA, ALKEM, IPCALAB, ABBOTINDIA trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their five-year medians: +7.5%, PLAYBOOK §7c) = 26.3x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. No growth or returns adjustment (sensitivity rows only). Bull 29x (its 75th-percentile forward P/E since Apr-2021, 29.1x); bear 20x (25th percentile, 20.0x): the range the market has actually paid, as in our Rainbow report.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value and ignores other income. Cipla's median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 is 15.9x (Screener); times the same 1.075 sector factor = 17.1x, rounded to 17x and applied to trailing EBITDA at the target date (Oct-2026 to Sep-2027 = half FY27E + half FY28E), with net cash at Sep-2027. Bull 17x (75th percentile 17.2x: the re-rated median already sits at the top quartile); bear 15x (25th percentile 15.1x).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at an 11.3% cost of equity, terminal growth 5.5%, plus net cash.
